nodes.label: Deterministic ACI miscoverage bound
nodes.rationale: (max(alpha_1, 1-alpha_1) + gamma) / (T gamma): smaller gamma gives a tighter long-run bound but slower adaptation — the trade-off is reported per gamma rather than a single gamma being asserted.

nodes.label: A13 · Change-point detector validation
nodes.rationale: Honest characterisation against ground truth plus synthetic injection; the operating point is reported, not asserted.

nodes.label: CUSUM ARL₀ operating point (k=0.5, h=5.0)
nodes.rationale: Empirical ARL₀ exceeds the 400-day simulation horizon at every h tested (right-censored), so h=5.0 produces essentially no false alarms. The binding constraint is detection delay, not false-alarm rate; h=5.0 is retained deliberately under the project's false-alarm thesis, honest for a small single-venue sample.

nodes.label: BOCPD benchmark
nodes.rationale: Kept as the principled benchmark but not shipped: a manager acts on '9 of 13 days below band since 12 May', not a run-length posterior, so CUSUM+persistence stays the production signal.

nodes.label: Synthetic level-shift injection (detection delay vs false alarms)
nodes.rationale: Larger δ detects faster and surer; lower h detects faster but admits more false alarms. A 0.5-band-unit shift sits near the noise floor and detects slowly — reported as an honest limit rather than tuned away.

nodes.label: Point deviation — per-day band check
nodes.rationale: Point deviation is the primitive and change-point the higher-order signal built on the same residual foundation; neither imports the other. nodes.label: SBC classification cutoffs (ADI ≥ 1.32, CV² ≥ 0.49)

nodes.label: ADI blind spot (obsolescence patterns)
nodes.rationale: ADI measures spacing between successive demands, so an item that sold densely for a short season then went dead classifies as non-intermittent. Declared as the Teunter-Syntetos-Babai case and put out of scope, since Croston lost on every node that did classify as intermittent.

nodes.label: Unanimous SBA selection is a property of the scheme, not the estate
nodes.rationale: With the cutoff at ADI ≥ 4/3, 2 − (3/2)(4/3) = 0 exactly, so the selection threshold is non-positive for every node at or above the cutoff while CV² ≥ 0 always: classified-intermittent entails selects-SBA by construction. 31 of 32 selecting SBA is therefore not a finding and must not be read as one.

nodes.label: CPTC theorem misstatement (Sun & Yu 2025)
nodes.rationale: The chapter claimed coverage 'guaranteed even as the venue's regime shifts'; CPTC proves exact coverage only under exchangeability, asymptotic time-averaged validity under a stationary state distribution, and faster post-shift convergence than ACI. 'An examiner can check it in ninety seconds.' Closed by replacing with Barber et al. (2023).

nodes.label: S5 group ICL negative result (Chronos-2 called with id='l1')

The fix produced a negative result, and a latent batching bug (the batch is the cross-learning group) would have made it a false positive without the catch.

nodes.label: TSB-AD (pinned VUS-PR metric, WP5)

nodes.label: vus>=0.0.6 fallback pin

nodes.label: Proactive briefing — ranked, de-duplicated, attributed daily feed (L1)

nodes.label: Transparent briefing rank score (source x severity x recency x novelty x baseline_trust x direction)

nodes.label: Change-point absorbs the deviation run and coincident stock flag

nodes.label: Correlational attribution — 'coincides with', never 'caused by'

nodes.label: Chat-log KB-gap (sop) signal — missing-SOP detection from unanswered repeats

nodes.label: Dormant-venue and non-live-data exclusions from the feed
nodes.rationale: Two River Taps is closed so its closure is dormant and generates no routine deviation items; checklist data is template-only, not live, so it is excluded rather than reported as if real.
nodes.norm_label: dormant-venue and non-live-data exclusions from the feed

nodes.label: A13 · Change-point / regime-shift detection
nodes.rationale: Complementary sustained-shift layer: point anomalies stay with /deviation/check, so the two layers do not compete for the same alert.

nodes.label: Standardised conformal residual stream z = (actual - DOW-median) / conformal half-band@90%
nodes.rationale: Standardising by the conformal half-band makes shift magnitudes comparable across venues with different scales.
nodes.norm_label: standardised conformal residual stream z = (actual - dow-median) / conformal half-band@90%

nodes.label: k-of-n persistence detector (4/7, abrupt)
nodes.rationale: Ellel is persistence-only because it is sparse and booking-driven, so CUSUM's drift assumption does not hold there (FLAG-CP2).

nodes.label: BOCPD benchmark detector
nodes.rationale: Kept as a benchmark rather than a production detector — it measures the two shipped detectors rather than serving alerts itself.

nodes.label: T4 recalibration loop — recalibration_needed flag
nodes.rationale: A confirmed shift makes the learned normal (DOW baseline + conformal calibration set) stale from the onset; the minimum shipped behaviour is a flag plus a degraded-confidence note until 28 post-change days accrue. Automatic re-fit on the post-change window is deferred (FLAG-CP3).

nodes.label: Leakage-free expanding one-step-ahead detection on trading days
nodes.rationale: Expanding one-step-ahead evaluation keeps future data out of the detection decision; restricting to trading days stops closures reading as shifts.
nodes.norm_label: leakage-free expanding one-step-ahead detection on trading days

nodes.label: Two River Taps closure as ground-truth structural break
nodes.rationale: The one shift with a known external cause, so it serves as the labelled positive against which detector latency (8 days, both detectors) is validated.
nodes.norm_label: two river taps closure as ground-truth structural break

nodes.label: A14 · Feature-enrichment ablation (Rung-3 GBM only)
nodes.rationale: Scope note leads the file because the verdict binds only the Rung-3 GBM and was repeatedly misread as a ruling on the exogenous set in general or on the served model.

nodes.label: Rung-3 GBM (baseline MASE 0.9551, 90% coverage 87.9%)
nodes.rationale: The only ladder model that consumes engineered features, which is why it is the only model this ablation can judge.

nodes.label: rung4_chronos2_exo — served Beer Hall model (rolling MASE 0.745)
nodes.rationale: Reaches covariates by a different mechanism (zero-shot conditioning through context/future frames) rather than engineered columns, so the GBM's negative verdict does not transfer; it carries weather live and earned its rung at the same gate.
nodes.norm_label: rung4_chronos2_exo — served beer hall model (rolling mase 0.745)

nodes.label: CHRONOS2_EXO_COLS — 15-column known-future exogenous set
nodes.rationale: 4 calendar + 1 event + 6 World Cup + 4 weather columns; widened from four calendar flags at G12.10b, after this ablation was written.

nodes.label: 90% model confidence set adoption rule (39 disjoint folds)
nodes.rationale: A column ships only if the 90% MCS EXCLUDES the baseline and retains the candidate, and coverage does not degrade by >3pp. Replaces the old >1% six-fold mean cut, which sat well inside fold-to-fold noise (ledger M24). The origin advances by a full horizon over the whole span because six folds is fewer than the moving-block length, which makes every bootstrap resample identical to the sample and pins every MCS p-value to 0 or 1.
nodes.norm_label: 90% model confidence set adoption rule (39 disjoint folds)

nodes.label: Constant-0 event feature in test folds (honest null, not a bug)
nodes.rationale: Only 7 local-event days fall in the active window and none in the recent rolling-origin test folds, so the event feature cannot change test MASE by construction; recorded as an honest null rather than a defect.
nodes.norm_label: constant-0 event feature in test folds (honest null, not a bug)

nodes.label: Weather train/serve consistency study (§4)
nodes.rationale: Named as the methodological contribution of the enrichment work: at inference only a forecast of weather is known, so the question is which TRAINING basis predicts best when SERVING on a forecast basis. Observed (ERA5) is an upper bound only, and the oracle (0.9005) is explicitly not achievable live.

nodes.label: leadmatched weather basis (forecast as issued 3 days ahead)
nodes.rationale: Serving basis for the study. Forecast skill at 3-day lead: temperature MAE 0.86 C (basis barely matters), precipitation MAE 3.55 mm (rain is where basis choice matters most).
nodes.norm_label: leadmatched weather basis (forecast as issued 3 days ahead)

nodes.label: Three training bases not separable on 39 folds
nodes.rationale: The 90% MCS retains observed, hindcast and leadmatched, so the lowest mean is marked as a ranking and 'best' is deliberately not written next to it.
nodes.norm_label: three training bases not separable on 39 folds

nodes.label: Honest negative verdict — no exogenous feature adopted into the GBM
nodes.rationale: Against a strong autoregressive baseline (lag-7/14, roll-28, DOW) every candidate increases held-out MASE: calendar flags are near-constant inside the test folds so they only add a spurious split, weather overfits ~270 training days, curated events have no test-fold anchor. Adoption is gated by evidence, and the enrichment's retained value is (1) a populated seam for deviation/change-point attribution and (2) the train/serve study itself (FLAG-FE1..FE10).
nodes.norm_label: honest negative verdict — no exogenous feature adopted into the gbm

nodes.label: A12 · Stock inventory days-of-cover reorder signal
nodes.rationale: Joins physical on-hand kegs to the A6 reconciled demand forecast. Beer Hall only because no TRT/Ellel stock sheets exist (FLAG-5).
nodes.norm_label: a12 · stock inventory days-of-cover reorder signal

nodes.label: Stock is a level, not a flow (FLAG-2)
nodes.rationale: Stock is a monthly level, so consumption is taken from the sales-side A6 forecast and never inferred from stock differences, which would confound deliveries, wastage and count timing.
nodes.norm_label: stock is a level, not a flow (flag-2)

nodes.label: Reorder rule: days_of_cover < lead(3) + safety(2)
nodes.rationale: Order target extends 7 days beyond cover. Lead and safety days are declared working assumptions for the owner to confirm per beer (FLAG-3), not measured values.

nodes.label: Size-aware keg-to-pints conversion (30 L -> 52.8, 50 L/unknown -> 88)
nodes.rationale: Refines A6's flat 88 pints/keg assumption (FLAG-4); the 50 L value is retained as the default for unknown container sizes.

nodes.label: NULL-demand lines surfaced as on-hand only, never a guessed cover
nodes.rationale: Only 1 of 14 core keg/cask lines maps to an A6 forecast node; the other 13 have no single mapped sales item or sit outside A6's top-k node set. The signal is exact where demand is known and silent where it is not.
nodes.norm_label: null-demand lines surfaced as on-hand only, never a guessed cover

nodes.label: Dead-stock / dead-listing candidates
nodes.rationale: Low mean quantity across many snapshots (or a single snapshot at high price) flags lines that occupy capital without turning.

nodes.label: Hand-typed footers stale; line-item sums authoritative (FLAG-6)
nodes.rationale: Feb/Apr/May footers are occasionally stale, so totals are recomputed from line items; the median keg-cost rise is mix-confounded and reported as indicative only (FLAG-7).
nodes.norm_label: hand-typed footers stale; line-item sums authoritative (flag-6)

nodes.label: A14b · Weather/calendar signal diagnostic (diagnostic only)
nodes.rationale: Asks whether the A14 L1 null hides a real category-level signal or weather is genuinely redundant-with-season. Explicitly diagnostic: nothing is adopted and the live ladder is unchanged.

nodes.label: Test A — L2/L3 weather ablation (aggregation hypothesis)
nodes.rationale: Weather clears the MASE+coverage bar at L2:Spirits, L3:Cider-BH and L3:Lager-BH — a localised, forecast-useful signal that L1 aggregation hides.
nodes.norm_label: test a — l2/l3 weather ablation (aggregation hypothesis)

nodes.label: Test B — physiology-matched weather features (beer_garden_day, temp_anomaly)
nodes.rationale: Raw weather (0.903) beats baseline 0.977 while the engineered forms do not; exo_temp_anomaly is fragile on ~1 summer of climatology (FLAG-WD1), so the beer_garden_day threshold is weighted more.
nodes.norm_label: test b — physiology-matched weather features (beer_garden_day, temp_anomaly)

nodes.label: Test C — calendar on transition-aware folds
nodes.rationale: Fold provenance matters (FLAG-WD3): a flat result on folds centred on term-vacation boundaries where the flag actually varies is real evidence the calendar is uninformative, whereas a flat result on A14's operational folds was not.
nodes.norm_label: test c — calendar on transition-aware folds

nodes.label: Test D — residual-on-weather OLS with AR partialled out (model-independent)
nodes.rationale: Called decisive because it is model-independent: incremental R-squared of weather over AR/season is >0 and significant at L1 (+0.042) and L3:Cider-BH (+0.023) on exo_temp_c, so weather is NOT purely redundant-with-season.
nodes.norm_label: test d — residual-on-weather ols with ar partialled out (model-independent)

nodes.label: Weather logged as a strong CANDIDATE for separate gated adoption
nodes.rationale: A real, forecast-useful signal was both localised and shown statistically significant, but adoption would need a covariate-aware model (TFT / TabPFN-TS, not a univariate foundation model) and its own gate, so nothing is adopted in this phase (FLAG-WD1..WD4).
nodes.norm_label: weather logged as a strong candidate for separate gated adoption

nodes.label: autoresearchclaw — PRJ93 critique-revise operating manual
nodes.rationale: Distilled from the AutoResearchClaw stage architecture so the full source analysis is not needed to run the loop. Not auto-loaded — must be named in the phase prompt. Where it conflicts with PRJ93_RULES.md, PRJ93_RULES.md wins and the conflict is flagged rather than resolved.

nodes.label: Five human gates (stop-and-ask)
nodes.rationale: Methodology change, dropping/adding a cited paper, rerunning an experiment, final figure types and any Overleaf push each stop the loop. One gate per question — never batched — so the human decision stays legible. Two further gates (evidence base before reading effort; research question before methodology) are candidates, not adopted, and must be raised rather than enforced. Never write outside brain/.

nodes.label: Critique-revise loop (draft -> 3 critiques -> synthesis -> revise -> test)
nodes.rationale: Hard cap of 2 revision rounds; on the third failure stop and report what still fails with a stated caveat.
nodes.norm_label: critique-revise loop (draft -> 3 critiques -> synthesis -> revise -> test)

nodes.label: One separate call per review role (no single-call multi-persona)
nodes.rationale: Three personas sharing a single context share every blind spot and cannot disagree in any load-bearing way — named as the single largest defect in the source system and the reason the loop is structured this way. Each role sees the draft section and its result files, and nothing from the other roles.
nodes.norm_label: one separate call per review role (no single-call multi-persona)

nodes.label: Fourth synthesis call — reconcile without flattening
nodes.rationale: Takes the strongest elements from each critique rather than compromising between them and preserves genuine disagreements, stating which evidence would settle a conflict. No role may veto; the synthesiser may discard a critique but must say it did and why.
nodes.norm_label: fourth synthesis call — reconcile without flattening

nodes.label: T1-T14 advance-vs-revise tests
nodes.rationale: Every test is pass/fail with no partial credit or judgement call, so the gate cannot be argued around. Any blocking failure means revise; advisory failures may pass with a stated caveat. T1-T14 are necessary, not sufficient — they catch defects but do not score against the DS591 rubric.

nodes.label: T1 — every number traces to a brain/log/*result*.md file
nodes.rationale: The load-bearing test: a number without a traceable source is the failure mode that destroys a dissertation's credibility and no amount of good prose compensates. If T1 fails, stop revising prose and fix the trace first. The path goes in a LaTeX comment beside the number.
nodes.norm_label: t1 — every number traces to a brain/log/*result*.md file

nodes.label: Failure and pivot signals (one signal, one action)
nodes.rationale: Each signal has exactly one prescribed action to be taken without deliberation. No-real-data is a hard stop overriding everything. Saturation and flat ablations mean the experiment design, not the writing, is the problem — raise a methodology gate. Identical byte-level metrics across conditions is a bug, never a null result. A revision under 80% of original word count is discarded because losing content silently is worse than not revising. A contradiction between sections is blocking and resolved before anything else.
nodes.norm_label: failure and pivot signals (one signal, one action)

nodes.label: Anti-patterns inherited from the source system
nodes.rationale: Computing a quality signal and not branching on it manufactures the appearance of rigour and is worse than no signal. Backfilling to hit a count makes the count carry no information. Degrading the hard stop into a 'proceed with a warning label' path converts the only real quality gate into a footnote — there is no graceful-degradation mode. Placeholder output survives into the artifact. Verifying without writing back means the uncorrected file is what gets submitted. Absence-by-grep is weak evidence and must be labelled an unverified negative.
nodes.norm_label: anti-patterns inherited from the source system

nodes.label: Adopted drafting rules (§7)
nodes.rationale: Claim bounding, statistical honesty (no superiority claim without a p-value; reframe as comparable where it does not win), honest retitling (an accurate title on a negative result marks better than an aspirational one), no invented numbers under pressure, and reimplementable method sections.

nodes.label: Role definitions are adapted, not validated
nodes.rationale: Distilled from a system whose own review stage was its weakest component and never run against a real PRJ93 chapter; the first use is to be treated as a trial and what the roles missed recorded in brain/ledger/phase_state.md. The file also cannot mark a draft, has no PRJ93 word targets, and does not know the project's state.
nodes.norm_label: role definitions are adapted, not validated

nodes.label: Drafting rules — long-form writing guidance
nodes.rationale: Adapted from AutoResearchClaw stage-17/19 prompt banks. Rules encoding a NeurIPS/ICML conference norm rather than a general writing principle are marked [venue-specific] and must be checked against 00_marking_criteria.md before being applied to PRJ93.

nodes.label: Evidence bounding — the full rule set (rules 1-6)
nodes.rationale: Titles may claim only what the tested conditions' numbers show; partial coverage takes 'Toward…' / 'Investigating…' framing. A single scalar with no condition labels supports no comparative claim. Never approximate a number from memory — if it is not in a result file it does not go in the text.
nodes.norm_label: evidence bounding — the full rule set (rules 1-6)

nodes.label: Statistical reporting rules (7-14)
nodes.rationale: 95% CIs on every table; p-values on every comparison with explicit non-significance wording; effect size alongside significance because a significant negligible difference is a finding about sample size, not method; both conditional and unconditional metrics where runs failed, since without both comparative claims are survivorship-biased; per-regime tables because aggregate-only results cannot support a robustness claim.

nodes.label: Method and setup reimplementability rules (15-21)
nodes.rationale: A baseline reported without stated tuning effort is a strawman and will be read as one. Generic labels (baseline_1, variant_2) make a results section uninterpretable. Evaluation metrics must be defined including the denominator, and preprocessing detailed enough to reproduce the input, not merely the model.

nodes.label: Structure and length rules (22-26)
nodes.rationale: Limitations in one 200-400 word section stating each point once, because repeating 'due to computational constraints' across sections reads as evasion. Roughly 80% of the text covers what was done and found. No body section dwarfing the others by more than ~3x; a results section shorter than related work signals a thin contribution.

nodes.label: Prose quality rules (27-30)
nodes.rationale: Hedging added during revision usually signals the reviser doubted a claim but did not check it — check it instead. Verb strength maps to evidence: 'demonstrates' needs significance across conditions, 'suggests' fits one condition, 'is consistent with' fits a non-significant trend. Introduction, discussion and conclusion must motivate, interpret and situate respectively rather than restate.

nodes.label: Citation practice rules (31-34)
nodes.rationale: Cite the originating paper, not a survey or later user. Citations clustered at the front signal that related work was written separately from the contribution. Reference-count targets (25-40, 15 in related work) are venue-specific and must be checked against 00_marking_criteria.md.

nodes.label: Figures and tables rules (35-38)
nodes.rationale: An unreferenced figure is a figure the examiner does not know why they are looking at. Per PRJ93_RULES.md a plain table is a defect unless the precise values matter more than the comparison. Never a placeholder in a cell — write N/A or drop the row.

nodes.label: Revision-specific rules (39-43)
nodes.rationale: A revision pass is targeted repair, not a rewrite: sections with no critique findings are copied verbatim, because rewriting untouched sections is how content and citations get silently lost. Abstract numbers must match the results section exactly, and an analysis that was not run is stated as not conducted rather than synthesised.

nodes.label: A7 · Onboarding-transfer (leave-one-venue-out)
nodes.rationale: Forecast = donor DOW shape x own level over a 14-day cold-start window used only to anchor the held-out venue's level; baseline is per-venue seasonal-naive on the same window so each per-venue comparison shares a denominator and is scale-fair.

nodes.label: LOVO harness — per-fold 7-day blocks with MCS + paired moving-block bootstrap
nodes.rationale: Scoring on consecutive 7-day blocks makes the comparison carry dispersion — a 90% MCS and a paired moving-block bootstrap CI on transfer minus naive, rather than a bare win count (ledger M23).
nodes.norm_label: lovo harness — per-fold 7-day blocks with mcs + paired moving-block bootstrap

nodes.label: G2 — venues do not share a ruler
nodes.rationale: Ellel admits no defensible scaled error, so it is scored on unscaled MAE in pounds and reported on its own; the loss column names each row's unit and rows in different units are not comparable. The earlier three-venue pool averaged pounds-denominated blocks with dimensionless MASE series, so its null was reached by an inadmissible route even though the direction was unchanged.
nodes.norm_label: g2 — venues do not share a ruler

nodes.label: calendar_lag7_active basis correction — both scaled rows now exceed MASE 1
nodes.rationale: On the basis the estate ruled, transfer scores 1.242 at the Beer Hall against 0.872 on the calendar_lag7 basis this module used to hard-code. Above one is worse than the seasonal-naive reference the denominator is built from, so beating the cold-window baseline is a statement about that baseline being poorer still, not about transfer being good. The denominator changed; the forecasts did not.
nodes.norm_label: calendar_lag7_active basis correction — both scaled rows now exceed mase 1

nodes.label: Withdrawn estate-level claim — a count over two venues carries no majority
nodes.rationale: Only 2 of 3 venues can enter a scaled comparison and one (Two River Taps) was closing at measurement, so the gate's original >=2-of-3 criterion is not evaluable. The per-venue rows stand individually; the estate-level claim is withdrawn on the grounds that the evidence base was never admissible, not weakened.
nodes.norm_label: withdrawn estate-level claim — a count over two venues carries no majority

nodes.label: Crossover sweep — transfer wins fall away as history accrues
nodes.rationale: Built to tell a partial-pooling story (transfer wins while the venue is data-poor, then hands over to its own seasonal-naive). The shape is still consistent with it, but at every window the denominator is 2, so the descent is a sequence of counts out of two and is equally consistent with one venue's behaviour plus noise. Reported as a description of two venues, not evidence for a cold-start regime.
nodes.norm_label: crossover sweep — transfer wins fall away as history accrues

nodes.label: Foundation-model rung — zero-shot chronos adopted over the global GBM
nodes.rationale: Rolling origin, 24 folds at horizon 7, paired within fold, zero dropped. Beer Hall 0.643 vs 0.760, Two River Taps 0.595 vs 0.811, both CIs excluding zero. Scored only where a scaled error is defensible (G2) and adoption requires a win at EVERY such venue, so one venue cannot carry the rung.
nodes.norm_label: foundation-model rung — zero-shot chronos adopted over the global gbm

nodes.label: In-context fine-tuning — forward note
nodes.rationale: The hand-built shape-transfer is the analogue of conditioning a held-out venue on the donor's shape; a foundation backbone with in-context fine-tuning would condition on the donor series directly, and the LOVO harness is exactly the test it must pass to be adopted.

nodes.label: Two-clause A7 gate (transfer NOT EVALUABLE, foundation PASS)
nodes.rationale: The two clauses are reported separately so neither can carry the other: the transfer clause needs a majority over three scaled venues and the estate supplies two, so it is NOT EVALUABLE; the foundation clause PASSES and is adopted. Overall verdict is governed by the transfer clause.
nodes.norm_label: two-clause a7 gate (transfer not evaluable, foundation pass)

nodes.label: Runtime identity stamp (.venv-forecast, Python 3.12.13, mps, store ceiling)
nodes.rationale: Environment, compute device, pinned library versions and the store ceiling (2026-07-07) are stamped on the result so a reported number is attributable to an exact runtime and can be reproduced or invalidated.
nodes.norm_label: runtime identity stamp (.venv-forecast, python 3.12.13, mps, store ceiling)
